account.title: Account
apikeys.expires_help: The key stops working on this date. You can't extend it; create a new key instead.
apikeys.org_help: The key works only in this organization, with at most your role there. You can't change this later.
apikeys.personal_empty: You have no personal API keys yet. Create one to use the CLI or an MCP client as yourself.
apikeys.personal_sign_in: Sign in to manage your personal API keys.
apikeys.personal_subtitle: Personal API keys let scripts and MCP clients act as you in one organization, never with more access than your role there. The secret is shown only once.
apikeys.revoke_body: Anything using {name} (…{hint}) stops working at once. This can't be undone.
apikeys.scopes_help: Pick only what the script or client needs. You can grant only what your role allows.
apikeys.scopes_pick_org: Select an organization to see the scopes you can grant.
apikeys.secret_warning: Copy this secret now — it will not be shown again.
apikeys.subtitle: Keys for machines that belong to the organization: org keys and project keys. Secrets are shown once. Your own personal API keys are in the account menu, under My API keys.

branding.contrast_low: Low contrast: the button text may be hard to read.
branding.display_name_help: Shown on sign-in pages and in emails. Leave empty to use the project name.
branding.logo_help: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 256 KB. Square images look best.
branding.logo_instant: The logo updates as soon as it uploads.
branding.logo_upload_failed: The upload didn't finish. Try again.
branding.preview_note: A close approximation of the sign-in page.
branding.storage_off: File storage isn't set up on this server, so logos can't be shown or uploaded. A logo you uploaded before is kept. Ask your operator to set up storage.
branding.subtitle: How your sign-in pages and emails look to end users.
branding.support_email_help: Optional. Shown to end users who need help signing in.
branding.title: Branding
clients.auth_method: How the app sends its secret
clients.auth_method_help: Use the header unless the app's library only supports the body.
clients.client_id_help: Your app sends this. It isn't secret.
clients.consent_implicit_warning: Only for your own apps. End users won't see what this app can access.
clients.delete_body: The app using this client can't sign end users in anymore, and its links are removed. This can't be undone.
clients.empty_body: Add one for each app that signs end users in: one for its website and one for its CLI.
clients.kind_native_help: Runs on the end user's computer. Has no secret.
clients.kind_web_help: Runs on a server and keeps a secret.
clients.localhost_warning: 127.0.0.1 is safer than localhost, which some systems resolve elsewhere.
clients.name_help: Shown to end users on the sign-in and consent pages.
clients.no_secret: No secret yet. This client can't sign in until you generate one.
clients.pkce_off_warning: Only for apps that can't send PKCE, such as a conformance test client. The app must then send a nonce on every sign-in.
clients.post_logout_help: Optional. Where end users land after signing out of the app.
clients.redirect_help_native: For example http://127.0.0.1/callback. Leave out the port: any port works.
clients.redirect_help_web: For example https://app.example.com/oauth/callback. For local dev, http://127.0.0.1:5100/… with the exact port.
clients.refresh_help: Lets the app stay signed in without asking the end user again.
clients.subtitle: Apps that sign end users in with this project.
clients.system_client_note: Othra manages this app. Its redirect URI follows the public URL and is updated on every start.
clients.system_note: Only the console app signs in here.
clients.title: OAuth clients
endusers.detail_subtitle_read: Read-only: you can see this person's sign-in methods, sessions, apps and tokens.
endusers.detail_subtitle_revoke: You can revoke this person's sessions, apps and tokens. Nothing else changes here.
endusers.disconnect_body: Its consents and tokens are revoked; access it already has ends within 15 minutes.
endusers.empty: No end users yet. They appear after their first sign-in.
endusers.methods_help: The email link and each linked upstream IdP. Only the person can change these, from their account page.
endusers.none_found: No end user matches that email.
endusers.sign_out_body: Apps signed in through it lose access, except offline access. The person can sign in again.
endusers.subtitle: People who signed in to this project's apps. You can view them and revoke their access.
endusers.title: End users

invites.drafts_hint: An assistant drafted these invites. Nothing is sent until you confirm.
invites.link_hint: Share this link if the email doesn't arrive. It is shown only now.
invites.new_link: New link. Share it if the email doesn't arrive:
invites.revoke_confirm: Revoke the invite for {email}? The link stops working.
invites.title: Pending invites
issuer.change_body: From {old} to {new}. Anything set up with the old URL stops working, and someone else may take the old handle.
issuer.check_failed: Couldn't check the handle. Try again.
issuer.discovery_help: Most apps need only the issuer URL or the OpenID Connect discovery URL.
issuer.handle_help: Part of the issuer URL. 3–40 characters: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not at the start or end. Unique across Othra.
issuer.locked_note: This project has OAuth clients or resource servers that depend on this URL, so the handle can't change.
issuer.subtitle: The URL that identifies this project to your apps and in the tokens it issues.
issuer.title: Issuer
issuer.unlocked_note: You can change the handle until the project has its first OAuth client or resource server. After that, it's locked.
issuer.url_help: Paste this into your app's OpenID Connect settings as the issuer.
keys.emergency: Key leaked? Rotate immediately with the CLI. Apps that cached the old keys may reject new tokens until they fetch the keys again.
keys.members_note: Only org owners and admins can rotate signing keys.
keys.no_active: This project has no active signing key, so it can't sign tokens. Rotate to create one now.
keys.no_active_member: This project has no active signing key, so it can't sign tokens. Ask an org owner or admin to rotate.
keys.retired_note: Retired keys are no longer published and are removed from this list after 30 days.
keys.retiring_help: No longer signs. Still published until {date}, so tokens it signed keep working.
keys.rotate_body: A new key is published now and starts signing tokens in about 10 minutes, so apps have time to fetch it. The current key then stays published long enough for the tokens it already signed to keep working.
keys.rotate_waiting: A new key is already waiting to take over at about {time}.
keys.rotated: New key {kid} is published. It starts signing at about {time}.
keys.rotated_active: New key {kid} is active and signs tokens now.
keys.subtitle: Keys that sign this project's tokens. Apps fetch the public keys from the JWKS URL.
keys.title: Signing keys
legal.acceptance_body: End users accept the current version the next time they sign in. Publish a new version when the meaning of your terms or privacy policy changes, not for typo fixes.
legal.bump_warning: Every end user of {project} must accept the terms again the next time they sign in. This can't be undone.
legal.clear_terms_body: Without a terms link, end users are no longer asked to accept. Past acceptances are kept.
legal.clear_terms_title: Stop asking end users to accept your terms?
legal.no_terms: Add a terms link to ask end users to accept your terms.
legal.no_terms_readonly: No terms link is set, so end users aren't asked to accept terms.
legal.privacy_help: Optional, but recommended. Shown next to your terms.
legal.subtitle: Links to your own terms. When a terms link is set, end users must accept it before they continue to your apps.
legal.title: Terms and privacy
legal.url_changed_hint: Changing the link doesn't ask anyone to accept again. If the terms themselves changed, use "Ask everyone to accept again".
links.empty: Not linked yet. Link one so it can ask for its scopes.
links.no_scopes: Add scopes to this resource server first.
links.none_left_resource_servers: Every resource server is already linked.
links.scopes_help: The client can ask only for these. Pick at least one.
links.unverified_note: This server isn't verified, so the client can't get tokens for it yet.
members.leave_confirm: Leave this organization? You lose access at once, and your personal API keys for it are revoked.
members.remove_confirm: Remove {name} from this organization? They lose access at once. They are signed out of the console and their personal API keys for this organization are revoked.
members.role_confirm: Change {name} from {from} to {to}? They get an email about it. If the role is lowered, they are signed out of the console.
members.subtitle: People in this organization and their roles. Owners and admins can change roles and remove people.
members.title: Members
onboarding.body: An organization holds your projects and your team. You can rename it later.
onboarding.project_note: We'll also create its first project, so you can add an app right away.
onboarding.title: Set up your organization
org.create_owned: You already own an organization, so you can't create another one.
org.none_body: You're not a member of any organization. Ask an admin to invite you.
org.none_title: You're not in any organization yet
org.slug_random_help: Leave empty for a random name like lunar-brass-5906. You can change it later.
org.subtitle: Pick an organization to manage its projects and members.
org.system_note: Othra manages this organization: it holds the console project, so its name and slug can't change.
org.title: Organizations
profile.name_hint: Shown to the people in your organizations. Leave it empty to show your email.
profile.not_a_person: This page is for people who sign in with a password. API keys and the basic login have no profile.
profile.password_changed: Your password was changed. Your other sessions were signed out.
profile.password_hint: Your other sessions are signed out.
profile.password_rules: At least 12 characters, not a common password, and not your email or name.
profile.sessions_body: Sign out of Othra in every browser and on every device, this one too.
profile.sign_out_confirm_body: You will need to sign in again on every device, this one too.
profile.title: Profile
profile.wrong_current_password: Your current password is not correct.
project.console_slug_help: Used only in console links. Changing it doesn't change your issuer URL.
project.read_only: Only org owners and admins can change these settings.
project.settings_general_subtitle: The project's name, ID and console URL name.
project.settings_hint: Name, issuer, branding, and terms and privacy.
project.slug_random_help: Leave empty for a random name like lunar-brass-5906. You can change it later.
project.system_general: Othra uses this name and slug for the console.
project.system_issuer: The console signs in through this issuer, so its handle can't change.
project.system_note: Othra uses this project to sign you in to the console. You can change its branding, terms, signing keys and upstream IdPs; Othra manages the rest.
project.title: Projects
rs.cimd_accept_help: MCP clients such as Claude Code sign in with a metadata document they host, without being registered here. End users always see a consent page that names the app's host. Turning this on also tells MCP clients that this project accepts them.
rs.cimd_apps_empty: No app has signed in this way yet.
rs.cimd_hosts_any: Empty means any host: anyone who can publish an https document can ask for this server's scopes.
rs.cimd_hosts_help: One host per line, for example claude.ai. Only apps whose client ID is on these hosts can sign in.
rs.cimd_locked: Verify this server first. Apps can't get tokens for a server that isn't verified.
rs.cimd_revoke_body: Every end user's access through {name} ends now. It can sign in again, with a new consent, unless you turn off apps without registration or remove its host.
rs.delete_body: Apps can't get tokens for {uri} anymore. This can't be undone.
rs.empty_body: Add your app's API or MCP endpoint so its clients can get tokens for it.
rs.failed_body: Apps can't get tokens for it. Fix the metadata, then verify again.
rs.http_locked: An http identifier can't be verified, so trust stays on.
rs.name_help: Shown to end users on the consent page.
rs.pat_dialog_body: This is the only time it is shown. Put it in your resource server's config. If you lose it, rotate the secret.
rs.pat_intro: End users can create fixed tokens for this server from their account page. The server checks each token at the introspection endpoint with its own credential.
rs.pat_locked_unverified: Verify this server first. Personal tokens work only with a verified server.
rs.pat_no_secret: No credential yet. The server can't introspect tokens until you generate one.
rs.pat_now_warning: A resource server still using the current secret can't check tokens from then on.
rs.pat_revoke_body: A resource server still using …{hint} can't check tokens from then on. This can't be undone.
rs.pat_revoke_title: Revoke the old introspection secret now?
rs.pat_rotate_body: You get a new secret now. The current one keeps working for the time you choose, so you can update the resource server first.
rs.pat_secret_intro: The server sends its ID and this secret to the introspection endpoint. You can't see a secret after it's created.
rs.pending_body: Not verified yet. Apps can't get tokens for it until it is.
rs.reason_blocked: The host resolves to a private address, which Othra doesn't fetch.
rs.reason_network: Othra couldn't connect (DNS or TLS error).
rs.reason_not_json: The response isn't a JSON object.
rs.reason_redirect: The metadata URL redirected. Serve it directly.
rs.reason_too_large: The response is larger than 64 KB.
rs.recheck_failing: The last {count} of 3 checks failed: {reason} After 3, apps can't get tokens for it.
rs.scope_description: What it lets the app do (optional)
rs.scopes_help: Permissions apps can ask for, for example devices:read.
rs.subtitle: APIs and MCP endpoints that accept this project's tokens.
rs.system_empty: Resource servers aren't used in the console project.
rs.title: Resource servers
rs.trust_body: Othra will issue tokens for it without checking that it belongs to you. Only do this for a server you run yourself.
rs.trust_help: For internal servers Othra can't reach. Othra won't check it again.
rs.trust_required: An http identifier needs this. Othra will issue tokens for it without checking that it belongs to you.
rs.trusted_body: Trusted without verification. Othra never checks it. Use this only for servers you run yourself.
rs.untrust_body: Turning it off sends it back to Pending. Apps can't get tokens for it until it is verified.
rs.uri_help: The URL of your API or MCP endpoint, exactly as your app checks it in the token, for example https://app.example.com/mcp. It can't change later.
rs.verified_body: Verified on {date}. Othra checks again every day.
rs.verify_help: Othra reads your app's metadata at this URL. It must list this identifier as resource and this issuer in authorization_servers.
rs.verify_passed: Verified. Apps can get tokens for it.
secret.body: This is the only time it is shown. Put it in your app's config. If you lose it, rotate the secret.
secret.close_disabled: Tick the box above to close.
secret.confirm: I've stored this secret somewhere safe
secret.label: Client secret
secret.title: Store this secret now
secrets.grace: Keep the current secret working for

secrets.now_warning: Apps still using the current secret stop working at once.
secrets.person_only: Only a signed-in person can create or rotate a secret.
secrets.revoke_old_body: Anything still using …{hint} stops working at once. This can't be undone.
secrets.rotate_body: You get a new secret now. The current one keeps working for the time you choose, so you can update the app first.
secrets.rotate_ends_old: The old secret …{hint} stops working now.

signin.client_id_help: From Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials.
signin.email_link_help: End users get a one-time sign-in link by email.
signin.email_locked: Turn Google on first: the email link is the only way to sign in.
signin.email_locked_system: The email link stays on for the console project: othra admin sign-in-link depends on it.
signin.email_locked_unlinked: Some end users haven't linked Google, so they couldn't sign in without the email link. Keep it on.
signin.enabled_help: Off hides the Google button on the sign-in page.
signin.google_intro: Let end users sign in with their Google account.
signin.google_locked: Turn the email link on first: Google is the only way to sign in.
signin.google_remove_body: End users can't sign in with Google until you set it up again.
signin.redirect_help: Add this exact URI under Authorized redirect URIs in your Google Cloud OAuth client.
signin.remove_locked: End users have linked Google, so it can't be removed.
signin.secret_help: Stored encrypted. It isn't shown again.
